data.name: Simeonel
data.gender_notes: Simeonel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Shimon, meaning 'God has heard'. In the Bible, Simeon is the name of two different figures: one of the twelve apostles and another an old man who saw the infant Jesus in the temple. In Christian history, Simeon Stylites (c. 390–459 AD) was a famous Syrian monk who lived on a pillar for over 40 years.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of deep faith and devotion to God.

in_hebrew.name: שמעונאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שמעונאל הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אל שמע' או 'אל שמוע', מבוסס על השם העברי שמעון, שפירושו 'שמוע' או 'להקשיב', ומוסיף את הסופית '-אל' שפירושו 'אלוהים' או 'אל'. השם שמעונאל מופיע בתקופת בית שני ומשמש כווריאנט של השם שמעון.

in_greek.name: Σιμεωνέλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Σιμεωνέλ είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα שמעונאל, το οποίο σημαίνει 'Θεός ακούει' ή 'Ακρόαση του Θεού'. historical_references.context: Asceticism and monasticism were popular practices among Christians during this period, with many seeking to live lives of extreme devotion and self-denial. Simeon's decision to live on a pillar for decades was an extreme expression of these practices.

historical_references.reference: Saint Simeon of Thessalonica, also known as Simeon the New Theologian, lived from approximately 949 to 1022 AD. He was a Byzantine monk and theologian, known for his mystical writings and teachings on prayer and the divine presence. The name 'Simeon' was also a common name during this period, and is of Hebrew origin, meaning 'God has heard'.
historical_references.context: During the Late Middle Ages, spirituality and mysticism became increasingly important in Christian thought and practice. Simeon's writings and teachings were influential in shaping the development of Orthodox Christianity in the Byzantine world.
